findings.reason: the author should derive the axis from the existing `component` segment class (or extend the existing HAS_PARENT edge-kind vocabulary) rather than mint a parallel one.
findings.text: §4 asserts "Nothing marks one as a member of a component set", but the grammar the consumer already pins declares `component` as its own segment class with its own vocabulary (`imas_standard_names/grammar/specification.yml` segment map → `grammar/vocabularies/components.yml`, as recorded by the plan's own reuse map), and imas-codex already models this: `Component.POLOIDAL`/`Component.TOROIDAL` with `physical_base`+`component` decompositions at imas_codex/standard_names/benchmark_reference.py:108-233 — the design proposes a new graph dimension without citing that the distinction exists one layer down

findings.reason: the plan should drop the catalog.yml carriage and rely on the pin plus the already-exported `arguments`/HAS_PARENT relation, which its own decision already requires.
findings.text: §5 item 5 proposes carrying the family grouping "into catalog.yml so the published sidecar exposes the family grouping the site needs", but the plan's own locked decision `the-name-is-the-decomposition` (2026-09-04) supersedes exactly that half and the reuse map cites plan:222-224 ("the catalog must consume the grammar by package pin rather than publishing a duplicate segment decomposition"); the sidecar owner already emits the family relation — `arguments` is built from HAS_PARENT edges (imas_codex/standard_names/export.py:1783-1788, doc "Exported as `arguments` in the ISN catalog format" at imas_codex/graph/models.py:5082) and the manifest writer at imas_codex/standard_names/export.py:2347 would gain a second copy of a derivable fact beside it

findings.reason: like any added public surface the section must account for what it replaces or why the existing `arguments` field cannot serve.
findings.text: §5 item 5 adds a field to the published `catalog.yml` sidecar (a public definition of the catalog schema, whose manifest model is `StandardNameCatalogManifest`) without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the substantive behaviour lands inside the ISN renderer (one rule) and the existing `sn` rename/supersede path; no proposal spreads complexity across parallel shallow spreads.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §5 item 5 re-emits a derivable family grouping into the published sidecar whose owner already exports the same relation, and the component distinction already exists in the grammar the consumer pins.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §5 item 5 adds a field to the published catalog sidecar (a public definition of the catalog schema) without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan ran a reuse map (docs/evidence/sn-grammar-refinement/reuse-map.md, 18 candidates, 18 verdicts) and its migration path extends existing verbs, but the design sections §4/§5 never cite the machinery that already carries what the "component axis" is meant to add, and §5 still carries a catalog.yml field its own locked decision retired.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the proposed shadow diff, parse/re-render and catalogue carriage route through the existing parser/composer and `persist_refined_name`; no wrapper over an existing mechanism without behaviour is proposed.
